judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 4 Indicators in Strand 1 NUMBER (same rank 0), so direction rests on substantive content. B4.1.1.3.3 requires determining the lowest common multiple (LCM) of two numbers up to 100 under the factors/multiples Content Standard; B4.1.3.2.1 requires comparing and ordering fractions by finding equivalent fractions using the Lowest Common Denominator (LCD), and its Learning Components explicitly name LCD-based equivalent fractions. Finding an LCD is the application of LCM to denominators, so proficiency with LCM supports success in the fractions indicator, not the converse. The shared tokens ('lowest','common') are not the basis of the judgment; the LCM-to-LCD skill dependency is. Noted limitation: both endpoints have truncated source evidence and the second endpoint's parent carries a documented Basic 4 Fractions code-mislabelling merge (printed B4.1.3.1 vs B4.1.3.2), and the second statement's 'like denominators' wording sits oddly with LCD use; this tempers confidence but does not undermine the LCM-to-LCD link.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (rank 1) under the same Content Standard B5.2.1.1 'Determine the pattern rule to make predictions about subsequent elements' in Algebra / Patterns and Relationships. B5.2.1.1.2 asks learners to describe a given pattern orally or in writing using informal mathematical language (one more, one less, five more, more/less than twice), while B5.2.1.1.7 asks them to write a rule in words and in algebra to represent a given pattern, with LCs separating the words-rule and the algebra-rule components. The pair-specific change is formalization: verbal characterization of a pattern's change is the informal precursor to stating a generalized rule symbolically, so proficiency in describing the pattern in mathematical language supports success in expressing it as a written and algebraic rule. Direction is same-rank but substantively supported by this informal-to-symbolic deepening rather than by code order alone. Evidence limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and both carry upstream audit/merge context, so the judgment rests on the bounded statement text, LCs, and shared hierarchy.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicator-grain statements, so the grain requirement is met: B5.2.1.1.8 (Grade BASIC 5, rank 1, Strand 2 Algebra, Sub-strand 1 Patterns and Relationships, under Content Standard B5.2.1.1) and B6.2.1.1.8 (Grade BASIC 6, rank 2, Strand 2 Algebra, Sub-Strand 1 Pattern and Relationships, under Content Standard B6.2.1.1). The audit/merge context for both endpoints and both parent Content Standards records that the identical wording with different official codes, grade scopes, and source segments denotes distinct grade-scoped curriculum items, not duplicate extraction, so the pair is legitimately two nodes. Substantively, however, the two indicator statements are verbatim identical ('Describe the relationship in a given table or chart, using a mathematical expression'), they share a single Learning Component whose skill text is that same sentence, and even the parent Content Standards are word-for-word identical ('Determine the pattern rule to make predictions about subsequent elements'). The bounded endpoint evidence therefore contains no deepening, extension, broadening, or increased complexity that would justify a developmental buildsTowards claim; the only differentiators are grade rank, code prefix, wording overlap, and a shared LC, none of which alone establishes developmental dependency. Increased algebraic formality visible in a neighbouring Basic 6 indicator (B6.2.1.1.7) appears only in a table-row context label and belongs to a different SFI, so it cannot supply endpoint-level evidence for this pair. What the evidence does support is meaningful, pair-specific recurrence of the same table/chart-to-expression pattern-description skill within the same Algebra pattern-rule sub-strand across adjacent grades — genuine instructional coherence and reinforcement rather than generic reusable overlap — so canonical symmetric relatesTo with null direction is the correct judgment; no_relation would understate the coherence and needs_review is unwarranted because the placement evidence is resolved and internally consistent. Material limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted source-evidence items each), so any differentiating exemplar detail outside the excerpt cannot be confirmed or ruled out; absence from this bounded excerpt is not proof of absence from the full source.

Same-rank direction is therefore grounded in statement content, not in code order or page proximity. Both endpoints have unresolved ancestry, so no hierarchy/domain inference was drawn from the framework-root fallback, and source evidence for both is truncated, which limits corroboration.
